scams.name: 'Guachimán' Yellow-Vest Watchmen Parking Extortion on the Tamarindo Strip
scams.description:
One traveler: 'IF YOU TRY TO PARK ANYWHERE IN TOWN AS A GRINGO — you will be harassed by scammers in yellow vests demanding you pay them to watch your car and keep it safe. Others will box you in with multiple vehicles and then demand you pay them to get out.' one traveler noted the harassment vanished when a native Spanish-speaking Latina was in the car. (April 2025).': 'Most lots will have someone who watches cars, throw them a couple hundred Colones and you're good'; cuts to it: 'They'll either make sure something doesn't happen or make sure something does.' One traveler: 'Guachimán = Watch man. It's a horrible disease… some are honest, some are plain scammers.'. one traveler's trick ('pay IF the car is safe — half the time they aren't there when we return') and at Manuel Antonio show the same operators on every tourist beach.

For travelers in 2025/2026, the defensive playbook: (1) keep a roll of ₡500 and ₡1,000 coins in the cup holder — ₡1,000–₡2,000 (~$2–$4) is the standard accepted tip and avoids escalation; (2) if the crew blocks the road or demands $10+ USD, that's the extortion version — don't hand over cash, roll the window most of the way up and creep forward (they always move, same as the Manuel Antonio Route 618 crews); (3) park ONLY in staffed paid lots — Plaza Tamarindo underground ($5/day), Cala Luna behind Diria, or the gravel lots near Langosta bridge — avoid unpaved shoulder pullouts; (4) never leave ANYTHING visible in the car because the 'watching' racket pairs with smash-and-grabs; (5) in golf carts remember keys are often shared across rentals — photograph your cart's ID number before walking off; (6) report extortion to the Tamarindo Fuerza Pública (town entrance, near the Monkey Bar turn) or dial 911 / tourist line 2511-9260.
scams.avoidance: Keep ₡500/₡1,000 coins in the cup holder — tip ₡1,000–₡2,000 (~$2–$4) before walking off. Park in paid staffed lots (Plaza Tamarindo $5, Cala Luna) — not unpaved shoulder pullouts. Never leave bags, phones, sunglasses, or electronics visible — guachis pair with smash-and-grabs. If extorted for $10+, roll windows mostly up and creep forward; don't argue roadside. Report extortion to Tamarindo Fuerza Pública (entrance to town) or dial 911 / 2511-9260.
scams.location: Main street of Tamarindo village (Calle Central / the road running parallel to Playa Tamarindo), the dirt lots behind Volcano Brewing / Witch's Rock Surf Camp, Playa Langosta access roads, and the gravel pullouts on the approach from Villarreal (Route 152)

scams.name: Beach-Hustler 'Surf Instructor' Lesson & $200 Board-Damage Ambush
scams.description:
And alongside them a beach-front ecosystem of freelancing 'instructors' the local cooperative openly calls a scam. Tico Times on X (Feb 2024). The classic sting has two variants. Variant A: approach on the beach, $40–$60 for a 'private' lesson, pay up front, instructor disappears or pushes you onto a damaged board and vanishes. Variant B is the canonical TripAdvisor case 'Beware predatory surf instructor William — San Jose, Costa Rica': instructor 'William' gave the traveler a board that was too small, steered them onto rocks at Langosta, then produced pre-existing scratches 'noticed' on the fins and pointed to the contract — $200 'damage fee.' As the traveler wrote: 'We've noticed some scratches everywhere on the board before renting it but they said it was just the coat, no need to put it on paper.' Parallel TripAdvisor thread 'SCAM ALERT — POLICE INVOLVED — Walter Surf Shop' (Jan 2020, still live 2025): 'Don't use this place. We were scammed and HELD UP before demanded to pay MONEY. We had to get the Police involved and luckily we are still alive.' (Feb 2025) mirror thread confirm the pattern into 2026. Going rate for a legit 2-hour lesson in 2025/2026 is $54–$85 pp (Viator via Iguana, Kelly's, or Witch's Rock includes board + rash guard + insurance); beach-hustlers quote $30–$50 with no paperwork, no photos, no insurance, and a surprise $200 'board damage' invoice.

For travelers in 2025/2026 trying Tamarindo's beginner-friendly river-mouth waves: (1) book ONLY through ICT-certified operators — Iguana Surf (iguanasurf.net, $84 group / $120 private), Kelly's Surf Shop (TripAdvisor 4.4, 120+ reviews), or Witch's Rock Surf Camp at Langosta — verify licenses at visitcostarica.com; (2) ask to see the instructor's ICT carnet and INS insurance policy before handing over cash; (3) before the first paddle PHOTOGRAPH every side of the board (top, bottom, both rails, nose, tail, fins) and text the photos to yourself with a timestamp — kills the 'damage fee' move; (4) refuse any verbal 'scratches are just coating, no paperwork needed' pitch — no paperwork means no insurance; (5) pay by credit card (Visa/Mastercard dispute > cash); (6) beach-hustlers almost always approach with a single board, no branded shirt, no shop-front — walk into an Iguana or Kelly's shop instead; (7) escalations: Tamarindo Fuerza Pública (2653-0283) or 24/7 tourist line 2511-9260.
scams.avoidance: Book via ICT-licensed schools — Iguana Surf, Kelly's Surf Shop, Witch's Rock Surf Camp ($54–$85 pp). Ask to see ICT carnet + INS insurance BEFORE paying; verify at visitcostarica.com. Photograph all sides of the board + text photos to yourself with timestamp before paddling. Pay by credit card (Visa/Mastercard) — cash has no recourse after a $200 'damage' invoice. Escalations: Tamarindo Fuerza Pública 2653-0283; tourist police 24/7 line 2511-9260.
scams.location: Playa Tamarindo main beach in front of the Diria, Volcano Brewing, and the Tamarindo river-mouth sandbar where beginners are taken; informal beach-front board-rental tents set up between Plaza Tamarindo and the estuary; Langosta rocks section for 'advanced' lessons

scams.name: Rental-Home & Airbnb Home Invasion — The Los Jobos Tamarindo Pattern
scams.description:
The US Embassy San José explicitly called this out in its November 25, 2025 Security Alert: 'Break-ins and armed robberies at vacation rentals have increased, particularly targeting foreign tourists.' The anchor case: Christopher Deir, a 40-year-old Canadian life coach from Toronto, was fatally shot during a home invasion at his rental house in the Los Jobos area of Tamarindo on July 11, 2025. OIJ reported that an intruder broke in; Deir's partner's screams drew him into the hallway where he was shot. (July 2025) anchors the discussion, with reposting the OIJ account verbatim.; robbers 'kept asking for the cocaine,' suggesting targeted scouted jobs.: 'a gang of thugs who have been terrorizing the area for months.': 5–6-flashlight invasion at a Playa Negra VRBO; the traveler's husband had locked the second-floor gate; Vrbo demanded they 'work it out with the property owner' who told them to 'watch their backs.' (April 2025) — Playa Grande — burglar took 3 laptops and $800 on day 2.: 'Costa Rica Tourism Police are actively investigating theft operations targeting tourists in Airbnb rentals, especially in coastal and popular tourist areas.' Mechanics: Airbnb/VRBO calendars leak arrival times; isolated villas are scouted; 4–6-man gangs breach a second-floor window 9 PM–2 AM.

For travelers in 2025/2026: (1) SKIP isolated beachfront villas — book inside a 24-hour guarded gated community (Hacienda Pinilla, Reserva Conchal, Langosta Beach Club) or a hotel with armed guards (Diria Beach Resort, Tamarindo Diria, Witch's Rock Surf Camp); (2) verify security BEFORE booking — message the host: 24/7 armed guard? Panic button? Patrol logs? 'Yes to all three' in writing is the minimum bar; (3) don't advertise arrival time on social media or let the Airbnb calendar show 'first night'; (4) on arrival confirm every door, window, and second-floor gate — pile furniture at weak points as did; (5) program 911 + OIJ 800-8000-645 + US Embassy San José 2519-2000 into speed dial; (6) if invaded: hide, call 911, don't confront — OIJ data confirms resistance correlates with shooting; (7) file at Tamarindo Fuerza Pública + OIJ within 24h for Vrbo/Airbnb refund and insurance claims.
scams.avoidance: Stay inside 24/7 guarded gated communities (Hacienda Pinilla, Reserva Conchal) or guarded hotels. Message host IN WRITING: 24/7 guard? Panic button? Patrol logs? 'Yes' to all three or skip. Don't post arrival dates to social media; ask host to calendar-block two days either side. Program 911, OIJ 800-8000-645, US Embassy San José 2519-2000 into speed dial on arrival. If invaded: hide, call 911, do NOT resist; file at Tamarindo Fuerza Pública within 24h.
scams.location: Rental villas and Airbnbs in Los Jobos (north Tamarindo), Playa Langosta gated sections, Playa Grande beachfront homes, Playa Negra south of Tamarindo, and any isolated beach-access Airbnb where the calendar shows arrivals online

scams.name: Rental-Car Relay-Theft & Main-Strip Smash-and-Grab outside Witch's Rock / Volcano Brewing
scams.description:
One traveler and wife — final lunch at Volcano Brewing/Witch's Rock Surf Camp in Tamarindo before their flight — parked 150 ft from their table on the main street, locked. Twenty minutes later their camera bag was emptied of $14,000 in pro camera gear + laptop + headphones — all neatly closed up again, bags untouched. Staff and police told them: RELAY THEFT. A thief with a signal-amplifier walks within 10 m of your table to capture the car's key-fob signal and relays it to an accomplice at the car who opens the keyless-entry locks without tripping the alarm. A Tile tracker in the camera bag was also stolen — these crews know exactly what they're looking for.: 'Never leave anything in your car, ever.' One traveler: 'En el carro nunca.' One traveler: 'plenty of warnings… whether it's a touristy area or not.' The lower-tech smash-and-grab pattern runs alongside: (June 2025) — one traveler's son's Beats stolen; One traveler: 'thefts of belongings in cars is probably one of the more common crimes… thieves wait and watch'; One traveler: 'Tico Times reported 2 girls went into a gas station and came back to their car and everything was gone. Just takes a minute or two.' (April 2025) corroborate: the 'watchman' crew and the smash-and-grab crew often share the same ecosystem.

For travelers in 2025/2026: (1) EVERYTHING of value goes in the hotel/villa safe — not the trunk, not 'hidden'; never leave cameras, laptops, passports, AirTag/Tile, wallets, or designer sunglasses in a rental car; (2) buy a Faraday key-fob pouch ($10 Amazon) BEFORE the trip — blocks the key-fob relay signal; put the fob inside when you sit down at Volcano Brewing; (3) use the key's physical-button unlock, NOT proximity — disables relay attack; (4) prefer paid/staffed lots (Plaza Tamarindo underground $5, Cala Luna, Calle Central Main Lot) over unpaved main-strip shoulder; (5) take a daypack into every restaurant, beach, and surf break — dry-bag-in-the-water rule applies; (6) if hit: file OIJ 800-8000-645 + Tamarindo Fuerza Pública within 24h — required for travel insurance (Amex Platinum, Chase Sapphire Reserve, Capital One Venture X all cover rental-car theft with a filed report).
scams.avoidance: NEVER leave valuables in the car — hotel safe only; treat every parking spot as compromised. Use a Faraday key-fob pouch ($10) + physical-button unlock instead of proximity unlock. Park in staffed paid lots (Plaza Tamarindo, Cala Luna, Diria) not main-strip shoulder pullouts. Waterproof dry-bag in the water with passport/phone/cash every surf; daypack into restaurants. If hit: file OIJ 800-8000-645 + Fuerza Pública within 24h for Amex/Chase/CapOne insurance.
scams.location: Main-street parking pullouts in front of Volcano Brewing / Witch's Rock Surf Camp on Calle Central Tamarindo, Banco Nacional / BAC Credomatic ATM lots, the gravel shoulders between Playa Tamarindo and Playa Langosta, and unattended rental-car spots while you surf for 2+ hours at the river-mouth

scams.name: LIR Shuttle / Pirate-Taxi Tamarindo Gouge — $80–$150 for a $55 Ride
scams.description:
The legit 2025/2026 shuttle economy Tamarindo ↔ LIR (Guanacaste / Daniel Oduber) is well-established: Tamarindo Daily Airport Shuttles and Interbus run shared shuttles ~$29–$45 pp pre-booked; private transfer LIR ↔ Tamarindo is $120–$135 1–4 pax (Tamarindo Shuttle, RideCR, Easy Ride); drive is 1–1.5 hours. Three scams run parallel. First, LIR arrivals-hall pirate taxis — non-orange unauthorized cars that crowd arrivals and quote $100–$150 for what should be $45 shared / $120 private; ride ends at a 'broken meter' argument and cash-only demand (traveler reports Jan 2024: 'in Liberia Costa Rica… $9 ride and the guy dropped us off and didn't complete the ride on the app. I got a charge over $30'). Second, hostel/beach-bar 'friend with a van' — (July 2025): local respondents warn 'old beat-up pirate taxis missing official logo and tags' and 'at worst they could rob you, or take a long route.' Third, the Tamarindo main-street red-taxi 'broken meter' trick — driver quotes ₡15,000–₡25,000 ($29–$48) for a ₡5,000 (~$10) in-town hop; One traveler: 'if a red taxi is using the meter and says it's broken, he's trying to scam you. Get out and try another.' Uber IS available in Tamarindo but is gray-legal — drivers ask you to sit up front. DiDi is a cheaper Guanacaste alternative.

For travelers in 2025/2026: (1) pre-book LIR ↔ Tamarindo via Interbus.com, Gray Line, Tamarindo Transfers, or Easy Ride — $29–$45 pp shared, $120–$135 private; save the confirmation email + driver name + vehicle plate BEFORE landing; (2) at LIR arrivals walk past 'taxi taxi' curb freelancers to your named-sign driver only; legit airport taxis are orange; (3) in town use Uber or DiDi (₡2,000–₡5,000 per hop) or RideCR pro service; (4) red taxis: say 'maría por favor' before moving; 'broken' = get out; MOPT LIR→Tamarindo range $85–$95 (above = scam); (5) Don't accept a 'friend with a van' pushed by the hostel — staff take commissions not safety audits; (6) solo women late: Uber or hotel shuttle, not a street taxi; file complaints at ctp.go.cr/inconformidades or call 911 / tourist line 2511-9260.
scams.avoidance: Pre-book via Interbus, Gray Line, Tamarindo Transfers, Easy Ride — $29–$45 shared / $120–$135 private. At LIR arrivals walk past 'taxi taxi' freelancers to your named-sign driver only. In town use Uber or DiDi (₡2,000–₡5,000 per hop) or RideCR pro service. Red taxis: say 'maría por favor' before moving; broken meter = get out; MOPT LIR→Tamarindo $85–$95. File complaints at ctp.go.cr/inconformidades or dial 911 / tourist police 2511-9260.
scams.location: Liberia Airport (LIR) arrivals curb, Tamarindo main-street taxi stands (Plaza Conchal, in front of Diria), and the informal 'friend with a van' networks touted at hostels and beach bars for SJO/LIR runs

scams.name: Tamarindo Banco Nacional / BAC ATM Skimming + Counterfeit-Bill Swap
scams.description:
A parallel thread 'Lost business visa in Tamarindo, Guanacaste Province ATM' (2024) anchors card-eating and retention fraud at the same ATM cluster. Traveler reports warns older expats to 'use BAC or BCR only, never Banco Nacional' and pull colones to avoid the DCC (dynamic-currency-conversion) upcharge. Three scams run: (1) card-skimming overlays on standalone strip-side ATMs — card data + PIN captured, cloned within days; (2) 'ATM ate my card' — device-level retention brackets prevent return, helpful 'stranger' observes your PIN re-entry; (3) the restaurant-adjacent counterfeit-bill swap, where change includes a torn or copied ₡10,000 or ₡20,000 note.: 'pay in colones (and beware of the "this bill is counterfeit" scam)' — driver swaps your real ₡20,000 for a pre-palmed counterfeit. Tamarindo beach-restaurant variant: tourist hands real USD $100; waiter returns saying bill is 'torn or marked' and demands a replacement. CR banks and shops DO legally refuse damaged US notes — but the quick-switch uses that real rule to swap your good bill for a genuinely torn one.

For travelers in 2025/2026: (1) withdraw cash only INSIDE a bank branch during business hours — Scotiabank, BAC Credomatic, BCR, or Banco Nacional lobby — not from standalone curb units; branches have guards and tamper-checked machines; (2) withdraw COLONES not USD — the USD option at ATMs runs DCC ~5–9% worse; max legal foreign withdrawal is ₡400,000/day (~$770); (3) pull ₡10,000 and ₡20,000 notes for daily spend — removes counterfeit-USD-swap exposure; (4) inspect every colón note handed back — legit ₡20,000 has a Carlos Luis Fallas Sibaja watermark and color-shifting thread; counterfeits feel plastic-smooth; (5) use a no-FTF credit card (Capital One Venture, Chase Sapphire, Amex Platinum) for restaurants and hotels, colones cash only for vendors and tips; (6) if you bring USD, bring only pristine post-2013 bills (CR banks reject torn/marked/pre-2013 notes by law); (7) if skimmed: freeze the card within 30 minutes, file at Tamarindo Fuerza Pública + OIJ 800-8000-645, save the ATM receipt as chargeback evidence.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs INSIDE bank branches during business hours (Scotiabank, BAC, BCR) — avoid curb units. Always withdraw colones not USD — decline DCC; saves 5–9% on every pull. Inspect every ₡20,000 note for Carlos Luis Fallas watermark + color-shift thread. Bring only pristine post-2013 USD bills; carry a credit card (Capital One, Chase, Amex) for restaurants. If skimmed: call bank within 30 min, file at Tamarindo Fuerza Pública + OIJ 800-8000-645.
scams.location: Banco Nacional ATM on the Tamarindo main strip (Plaza Tamarindo), BAC Credomatic ATM at Plaza Conchal, Scotiabank ATM between Diria and the roundabout, and adjacent street-side change booths near the main strip / restaurant cluster

scams.name: Tamarindo Nightlife Drink-Spiking & 'Sexpat' Prostitution-Ring Extortion at the Casino
scams.description:
One traveler: 'Sexpat grifters all over Guanacaste these days. The whole region is really fucked up and not what it once was. There are plenty of drug gangs and prostitution rings that have moved into the area as well.': 'Avoid tamarindo at all… tamarindo and jaco are gentrified and that's the main reason prostitutes are all over the place.'.: a CR condo developer told him of a tourist who brought a woman home — next morning she demanded $500 and refused to leave; manager's advice: 'pay her, or else her boyfriend or pimp could come after him.' One traveler: 'In Jacó bartenders and dancers often prostitute themselves to gringos, sometimes without them actively agreeing to hire them… next morning she will threaten to call her pimp if you don't pay her $500. Tamarindo is a tourist town just like Jacó.' One traveler: woman he met kept 'eyeing my phone' and 'tried to force herself to stay the night'; sending her home broke the pattern.: 'Avoid the casino unless you want to lose all your cash, realize you've been pick pocketed going to the ATM, and maybe get roofied.' Drink-spiking with scopolamine ('burundanga'), ketamine, or benzos is documented by NZ MFAT and Australian Smartraveller advisories for CR. Prostitution is legal between consenting adults over 18; the pimp-backed 'pay or my boyfriend comes for you' extortion is not.

For travelers in 2025/2026: (1) never accept a drink from a stranger already at the bar — buy your own and watch it poured; use Nightcap / SipChip test strips ($12 Amazon) if uncertain; (2) if you meet someone who needs 'somewhere to stay,' decline and book them an Uber home — One traveler: 'if you aren't into it send her home in an Uber'; (3) if pressed for $500 next morning, refuse, pack, leave; call 911 not pay — pimp threats are usually bluffs; (4) Costa Rican hotels require cédula (ID) for every overnight guest — a partner who won't show cédula is a red flag; (5) at the casino, cash the bare minimum chips you're willing to lose; never walk to the ATM drunk — use the in-hotel ATM at Diria under camera; (6) the unlit beach path between Monkey Bar and Langosta is a documented mugging corridor — take an Uber or walk the main road; (7) emergency: 911, US Embassy 2519-2000, Tamarindo Fuerza Pública — file drink-spiking WITHIN 6 HOURS (toxicology window).
scams.avoidance: Buy and watch your own drinks; carry Nightcap/SipChip test strips if uncertain. Anyone asking to stay the night — Uber them home; decline and still enjoy the date earlier next day. Demand cédula at any hotel check-in; a refusal = leave; Costa Rican law requires it. If extorted for $500: refuse, pack, call 911 + US Embassy 2519-2000 — don't pay. Drink-spiking: file at Fuerza Pública within 6h for toxicology + OIJ + travel-insurance claim.
scams.location: Monkey Bar / Crazy Monkey nightclub district, the Tamarindo Diria casino, Sharky's Sports Bar, beach-front DJ bars between Plaza Tamarindo and the river-mouth, and 'date back to Airbnb' routes through the unlit beach path to Langosta
